rules.text: In the App Router, pages and layouts are Server Components by default. Add `"use client"` only to the component that needs state, event handlers, effects or browser APIs, as far down the tree as you can, never to a whole page or layout.

Only environment variables named `NEXT_PUBLIC_...` reach the browser, and their values are built into the JavaScript bundle. Never give a secret that prefix. Read secrets only in server code, and start each module that reads one with `import 'server-only'`.

Fetch data in Server Components where you can, and pass it down as props. In a Client Component, read a promise passed from the server with `use`, or use the data library the project already has, such as SWR or React Query. Do not write your own fetching in an effect.

Run Python and its tools through the project's environment: `uv run`, the virtual environment's own `python`, or `python -m <tool>`. Never install packages into the system Python with a bare `pip install`.
Declare a dependency in the file the project already uses, `pyproject.toml` or a requirements file, never only in an install command. Ask before adding one (R-CODE-006).
Open text files with an explicit encoding, such as `open(path, encoding="utf-8")`. Python's default encoding depends on the platform and its locale.
Catch the specific exceptions you expect, such as `OSError` or `ValueError`. Never write a bare `except:`, and never catch `Exception` only to pass.
Pass `subprocess` commands as a list of arguments. Never use `shell=True` with text you did not write yourself.
Run tests with the runner the project already uses, `python -m pytest` or `python -m unittest`, from the project root. Name test files `test_*.py`, and keep them where the project keeps its tests.

Call hooks only at the top level of a component or a custom hook: never inside a condition, a loop or a nested function, and never after an early return. Name a custom hook `use` followed by a capital letter, such as `useCart`.
Give each item in a rendered list a `key` that comes from the data, such as an ID. Never use the array index as the key when items can be added, removed or reordered.

Do not use an effect to compute values from props or state, or to respond to a user event. Compute such values during render, and handle events in their handlers. Use effects only to sync with something outside React.
Never change state or props in place. Make a new object or array, such as `{ ...user, name }` or `[...items, item]`, and pass it to the setter.
Run the project's type check, its `typecheck` script or `tsc --noEmit`, before you call a step done. Never loosen `tsconfig.json`, such as turning off `strict`, to make errors go away.

Never silence a type error with `any`, `@ts-ignore` or a `!` non-null assertion. Use `unknown` and narrow it, or fix the type. If a suppression is truly needed, use `// @ts-expect-error` with the reason on the same line.

Treat data from outside the program, such as JSON from the network, files, environment variables and user input, as `unknown`, and check its shape before you use it. A type assertion with `as` checks nothing at runtime.

Install packages with the package manager whose lockfile the project has: `package-lock.json` means npm, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pnpm, `yarn.lock` Yarn, and `bun.lock` Bun. Commit the lockfile change with the dependency change, and ask before adding a dependency (R-CODE-006).
